title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: In 2025, GOAL’s Programme Innovation Lab supported country teams to deliver stronger impact amid shrinking humanitarian budgets, shifting from generating “new ideas” to helping programmes adopt evidence‑informed, scalable solutions aligned with GOAL’s Crisis to Resilience framework. A key achievement was the continued growth of the Humanitarian Innovation Fund, which reached €270,000 and enabled investment in high‑impact digital and system‑strengthening innovations. Several initiatives advanced from concept to practical use: in Ethiopia, Zcalc and the MOYO chart simplified malnutrition screening for low‑connectivity settings; in Niger, a community-based digital early‑warning and response system reached 158,890 people across 107 communities; and in Sierra Leone, ANCHOR—an AI‑enabled platform integrating WhatsApp reporting—supported Mpox response and is poised for wider replication. Across all contexts, the Lab reinforced a central lesson: innovations scale successfully when designed for low‑resource realities, aligned early with national systems and strengthened through trusted technical partnerships.. Climate change affects the social and environmental determinants of health and crises that affect health systems are increasingly caused by and related to climate change - for example through changes to disease outbreak patterns including malnutrition, malaria, diarrhoea, cholera, heat stress and through direct damage to health infrastructure. Innovations to strenghten the capacity of health systems and infrastructure will support national and state health systems build resilience and adapt to climate change and the changing and increasing demands placed on them.
